const pair = $('🔁 Process Pairs').first().json;
const res  = $input.first()?.json || {};
return [{ json: {
  seq: pair.seq || 0,
  isPair: pair.isPair === true,
  tier: pair.tier || 'none',
  score: pair.score || 0,
  primaryId: pair.primaryId || null,
  secondaryId: pair.secondaryId || null,
  primaryLabel: pair.primaryLabel || null,
  secondaryLabel: pair.secondaryLabel || null,
  reasons: pair.reasons || [],
  primaryUrl: pair.primaryUrl || null,
  secondaryUrl: pair.secondaryUrl || null,
  outcome: res.error ? 'failed' : (res.outcome || (pair.tier === 'auto' ? 'merge_dispatched'
            : pair.tier === 'review' ? 'approval_sent'
            : pair.tier === 'deferred' ? 'deferred' : 'logged')),
  detail: res.error ? String(res.error.message || res.error) : (res.detail || null),
} }];

parameters.content:
## 20 · DUPLICATE DETECTOR (sub-workflow)
Full-scan, blocking-key matcher with an explicit confidence score.

**Why a full scan and not a delta?**
A duplicate is very often an *old* record nobody has touched in two years.
A last-modified window would never see it. Hygiene runs delta; dedup runs full.

**Why static data instead of passing items?**
Records are pooled in workflow static data while paging, so memory stays flat.
Passing 10 000 records through a loop item-by-item is what makes n8n dedup
templates fall over at scale.

Default ceiling: `maxRecordsForDedup = 10 000`. Above that, raise it and give
the n8n instance more memory, or shard the scan by lifecycle stage.

## Confidence model — this is what you are selling
Every pair gets a score and a plain-English reason list that goes straight
into the Slack approval card.

| Score | Contacts | Companies |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | identical normalised email | identical web domain |
| 90 | same E.164 phone + last name | — |
| 88 | full name + corporate domain | name + country |
| 80 | full name + company | — |
| 74 | — | legal-suffix-stripped name |
| 72 | initial + last name + domain | — |
| 68 | — | name tokens + city |
| 58 | last name + company | — |

**Penalties** role mailbox −30 · different countries −8 · different emails −5
· **two different company domains caps the score at 40** (near-certain they are
different companies).

Only a **100** can auto-merge, and only for object types listed in
`autoMergeObjects`. Everything else needs a human.

### Transitivity is deliberately limited
Union-find clustering runs **only on 100-score links**. If A=B and B=C by exact
email, A/B/C collapse into one survivor in a single pass.

Fuzzy links are never chained. Chaining "same last name + same company" would
merge four different people at Acme called Smith. Fuzzy pairs stay pairs, and
each one is judged on its own.

`maxBlockSize` (60) skips blocking keys with too many members — that is the
signature of a placeholder value like a blank last name, not of 300 duplicates.

### Kill switch
`maxMergesPerRun` (default 50) caps irreversible actions per run. Pairs over
the cap are **deferred**, not flooded into Slack — they merge on the next run.

A first run against a dirty 40 000-record database therefore takes a few
nights, on purpose. That is the feature, not a limitation.
